# Specification {#sec-specification}

This appendix reproduces the specification (*cahier des charges*) of the thesis as rewritten for the final report, preceded by the summary of the problem it addresses. It differs from the official specification of 25 February 2020 mainly in naming no specific graphics library, where the official one names LittlevGL, and in adding keyboard support to the mouse support the official one asks for.

## Problem summary {#sec-problem-summary}

*Smart Object Oriented* (SOO) technology, developed by the REDS institute at HEIG-VD, lets running operating systems (OS) migrate across a set of interconnected embedded systems. It introduces the notion of a *Smart Object*, an embedded system such as a Raspberry Pi 4, and of a *Mobile Entity* (ME), the running OS that migrates.

One of the main targets of SOO is home automation, the use of computing to control the installations of a building. Letting an ME show a graphical user interface, on a touchscreen for example, opens the door to many kinds of applications. With such an interface, users could view the data an ME manages, such as weather readings, and also interact with it, for example to change settings or to view the data in another form.

The goal of this Bachelor thesis is therefore to add support for graphics and input devices to SO3, an OS developed by REDS and used as the basis for MEs. An existing graphics library must be integrated into SO3, first when it runs standalone. Then, an ME based on this new version of SO3 must be created and integrated into the SOO framework. Development starts in an emulated environment, and must then be deployed on a Raspberry Pi 4.

## Requirements {#sec-requirements}

### SO3 {#sec-requirements-so3}

Development takes place on the ARM Versatile Express platform, emulated by QEMU.

#### Graphics library {.unnumbered}

An existing graphics library must be chosen and placed in SO3's user space. The library must be integrated into SO3's build system so that SO3 applications can use it.

A demo application must be written, to test the work done during this thesis and to show what the library offers, such as its graphical elements.

#### Writing drivers {.unnumbered}

##### Framebuffer {.unnumbered}

A controller providing a framebuffer must be found on the emulated platform, and a driver written so that SO3 can detect and use this controller to display a graphical interface on screen.

##### Input devices {.unnumbered}

Again, the controller or controllers that communicate with the keyboard and the mouse must first be found. Then, their drivers must be written, so that the events generated by the keyboard and the mouse can be retrieved.

#### Adapting SO3 {.unnumbered}

To control and query these drivers, some system calls of the SO3 kernel must be adapted or created. For example, it must be possible to write to the framebuffer's memory, or to retrieve the mouse coordinates.

This communication with the drivers must also be possible from an SO3 application: the modified system calls must be callable from user space.

### SOO {#sec-requirements-soo}

This second part aims to create an ME based on SO3 that SOO can use. This ME must include the changes made in the first part. Development takes place on the ARM Versatile Express platform emulated by QEMU, but SOO and the ME must also be deployed on a Raspberry Pi 4. This part consists of several steps.

#### Developing the virtual interfaces {.unnumbered}

MEs have no direct access to the hardware: SOO acts as the intermediary between the ME and the hardware, through virtual interfaces. These interfaces require development on both the ME (SO3) side and the SOO side.

Two virtual interfaces must therefore be developed: one for the framebuffer, and one for user input (keyboard, mouse, touchscreen).

#### Porting to the Raspberry Pi 4 {.unnumbered}

The changes made to the ME and to SOO must be ported to the Pi 4 where needed. Although the Pi 4 has an ARM processor, its architecture is very different from the Versatile Express platform, and it has other controllers.

To test the integration of the graphics library and the support for input devices, several touchscreens will be chosen and proposed to REDS for purchase. The screens must be tested with the new ME, and support for touch events must be added too.
